stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the object arrow $\overline{AB}$ along the axis. Three characteristic rays leave $B$ and construct the image $\overline{A'B'}$. Watch the image flip through infinity as $\overline{AB}$ crosses the focal point $F$.
stages.concept: Thin-lens conjugation: $\frac{1}{\overline{OA'}} - \frac{1}{\overline{OA}} = \frac{1}{f'}$. Magnification: $\gamma = \frac{\overline{OA'}}{\overline{OA}}$. Sign convention: real object $\overline{OA} < 0$; converging lens $f' > 0$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Place the object $\overline{AB}$ so its image $\overline{A'B'}$ lands on each dashed target arrow. The three rays stay visible — use them to line up the image, then press Fire (or Space) to confirm. Light all 3 targets in 5 shots.
stages.concept: Each target specifies both a position $\overline{OA'}$ and a magnification $\gamma$. Only one object position $\overline{OA}$ satisfies both simultaneously.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Rays and image are hidden — only the object and the dashed target arrows remain. Read $\overline{OA'}$ from each target's base, compute the required $\overline{OA}$ from the conjugation formula, drag $\overline{AB}$ to that spot, then Fire. You have one shot per target.
stages.concept: Invert the formula: $\overline{OA} = \dfrac{1}{\,\frac{1}{\overline{OA'}} - \frac{1}{f'}\,}$. Convert the axis reading to centimetres, apply the sign convention, then compute.

labels.exhausted: OUT OF SHOTS · RESET TO RETRY
labels.tip2: align the image with the target, then press SPACE
labels.tip3: compute OA from the target, set AB, then fire
labels.strategy: OA = 1 / (1/OA' − 1/f'). Read OA' from target base on axis.

1.1: Grab the object arrow and slide it left or right along the horizontal axis.
1.2: F and F' are the focal points, both 20 cm from the lens. Watch what happens as AB crosses F.
1.3: When OA < −f' the image is real and inverted on the right. When −f' < OA < 0 the image is virtual and upright on the left.

2.1: Each dashed arrow tells you where the image should land — same base position on the axis, same size, same orientation.
2.2: Slide AB while watching the constructed A'B' — align the base of A'B' with the base of the target, then press Fire.
2.3: Farther object → smaller closer image. Object at 2f' → image at 2f' with γ = −1. Closer to F → larger farther image.

3.1: The dashed target arrow's base tells you OA'. Read its x-coordinate, subtract the lens's x-coordinate, then convert to cm using the axis scale.
3.2: Apply 1/OA' − 1/OA = 1/f' with f' = 20 cm. Solve for OA: OA = 1 / (1/OA' − 1/f'). Remember OA is negative for a real object.
3.3: Drag AB to x = 400 + OA·(px/cm). Use Peek to verify your current OA in the sim matches your paper calculation, then Fire.
